'''''Lycium afrum''''', the '''kraal honey thorn''' ([[Afrikaans]]: '''kraalkriedoring''') is a [[shrub]] in the potato [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] ([[Solanaceae]]), indigenous to the [[Western Cape Province]], [[South Africa]].<ref>http://redlist.sanbi.org/species.php?species=2846-2</ref>

==Distribution==
The species is native to the far western limits of the [[Western Cape Province]] in [[South Africa]]. It occurs from Clanwilliam in the north, southwards to the Caledon area, and westwards into the [[Cape Peninsula]].<ref>Venter, A.M. (2000). Taxonomy of the Genus ''Lycium'' L. (Solanaceae) in Africa. Thesis (Ph.D. (Botany and Genetics))--University of the Free State. https://scholar.ufs.ac.za/handle/11660/1960?show=full</ref>

It has appeared in [[Australia]] and is regarded with some concern as possibly invasive. Australian government factsheets remark that in Australia it is an uncommon hedge plant, sparingly naturalised in a few areas in Victoria.<ref name="efsa">{{cite web|title=*Lycium afrum|url=http://www.flora.sa.gov.au/efsa/lucid/Solanaceae/Solanaceae%20species/key/Australian%20Solanaceae%20species/Media/Html/Lycium_afrum.htm|website=eFloraSA|publisher=Government of South Australia|access-date=8 December 2017}}</ref>

==Description ==
''Lycium afrum'' is a moderate-sized shrub that may grow as high as {{convert|3|m}} and is formidably armed with straight, woody [[Thorns, spines, and prickles|thorn]]s.

Its leaves are leathery and tufted on short shoots.

It bears tubular purple flowers {{convert|12|-|20|mm}} long, with flared petals about one quarter the length of the tube.<ref name= "JManningFB">{{cite book | last = Manning | first = John | title = Field Guide to Fynbos | publisher = Struik Publishers | location = Cape Town | year = 2008 | isbn = 9781770072657 }}</ref>

The fruit is a subspherical berry, very dark red when ripe, eaten by birds.

It is not clear how safe it is to eat the fruit, though berries of some species of ''Lycium'' certainly are eaten with impunity by humans and animals.<ref name= "WattPP">Watt, John Mitchell; Breyer-Brandwijk, Maria Gerdina: The Medicinal and Poisonous Plants of Southern and Eastern Africa 2nd ed Pub. E & S Livingstone 1962</ref>
